The week is a standard unit of time consisting of seven days, commonly used in many cultures around the world. The concept of a week has its origins in ancient civilizations and has been adopted in various forms by different societies. Each day of the week is typically associated with specific activities, cultural practices, or historical significance.

The weekend specifically refers to the last part of the week, traditionally encompassing Saturday and Sunday. This period is often designated for rest, leisure activities, and social gatherings, providing a break from the regular workweek. The concept of the weekend varies across cultures; for instance, in some countries, the weekend may fall on Friday and Saturday, while others may observe different days altogether.
